payload.title: Australian Wedding Ceremony Script With the Legal Wording
payload.excerpt: An original Australian wedding ceremony script with the section 46(1) monitum and section 45(2) vow quoted from the Marriage Act 1961, every part marked legally required or optional, plus witnesses, signing and marrying overseas. General information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
key_takeaways: A celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination says the section 46(1) monitum, or words to that effect, before you marry, in front of your witnesses.
With a celebrant who is not a minister of religion, each of you says the section 45(2) vow, or words to that effect, and your own vows can sit beside it.
An authorised celebrant must be physically present with the two of you and 2 witnesses over 18, and all of you sign 3 marriage certificates on the day.
An Australian celebrant cannot perform a legal marriage overseas, so a celebration abroad pairs with a legal ceremony at home or follows the destination's own law.

faq.q: What does a celebrant legally have to say in Australia?
faq.a: A celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination says the section 46(1) monitum before you marry, beginning "I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law", or words to that effect. With a celebrant who is not a minister of religion, each of you then says the section 45(2) vow to the other, or words to that effect.

faq.q: What is the monitum in a wedding ceremony?
faq.a: It is the statement in section 46(1) of the Marriage Act 1961 that a celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination says to you, in front of your witnesses, before you marry. In it, the celebrant states they are duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages, reminds you of the solemn and binding nature of the relationship you are about to enter, and says what marriage is according to law in Australia. The full wording is quoted above.

faq.q: Can we change the legal vows?
faq.a: Both the vow and the monitum allow "words to that effect". Ask your celebrant before you change a word, and add your personal vows beside the legal line rather than in place of it.

faq.q: How many witnesses do we need at an Australian wedding?
faq.a: At least 2, who are or appear to the celebrant to be over 18. They are present for the ceremony and sign the 3 marriage certificates with you and your celebrant.

faq.q: Does a religious ceremony need the monitum?
faq.a: Section 46(1) applies to celebrants who are not ministers of religion of a recognised denomination. Under section 45(1), a minister of religion may solemnise a marriage according to any form and ceremony recognised as sufficient by their religious body or organisation. Ask your minister which words their ceremony uses.

faq.q: Can our Australian celebrant marry us overseas?
faq.a: No. An overseas marriage cannot be performed by an Australian-authorised marriage celebrant. Couples marry under the destination's law, or marry legally at home and hold a symbolic ceremony abroad.
